rows.label: Finish two Physical Education courses before you graduate
rows.note: Credit can also come from a varsity team or marching band, which the board cannot see, so check this yourself.

rows.label: Pass the university swim test (or finish two Beginning Swimming classes)
rows.note: Two Beginning Swimming classes (PE 1100 or PE 1101) with the instructor's recommendation also satisfy it.

rows.label: Clear any conduct sanctions before graduating; unpaid university bills can delay your diploma
rows.note: Open conduct sanctions or a pending conduct complaint hold up the degree itself. Unpaid financial obligations do not stop the degree or transcript access, but the diploma may be held.

rows.label: Earn at least 120 academic credits (AP and test credit may be included)
rows.note: Physical Education, the 1000-1099 supplemental courses, courses numbered 4980 (except in CHEM, HADM, PUBPOL, SOC and STSCI) and ELSO courses are left out, following the Arts & Sciences registrar's list of courses that earn no academic credit; at most 12 ROTC credits count. The long list of individually named no-credit courses is not encoded, and neither are other courses that earn no degree credit (remedial, precalculus, repeats, forbidden overlaps), see the no-credit check below.

rows.label: Make sure the 120 credits leave out courses that give no degree credit

source.anchor: Courses that do not count toward the 120 credits required for the degree

rows.note: Teaching assistant service, remedial work, precalculus, supplemental science and math, Learning Strategies Center and ESL courses, repeats and forbidden overlaps earn nothing. So does a course that is a prerequisite for one you already finished, and many individually named courses on the registrar's list (the board does not check those; look at that list).

rows.label: At least 100 of the 120 credits must come from Arts & Sciences courses taken at Cornell (no AP, IB, test or transfer credit)
rows.note: AP, IB, test and transfer credit, and most courses from other Cornell colleges, do not count toward the 100. These do count: approved full-time semester or year study abroad (not summer), some off-campus Cornell residential programs, up to three other-college courses your major accepts, and A&S summer session courses.

rows.label: At least 80 credits must be taken for a letter grade
Complete the minimum full-time semesters in residence: six for first-year entrants and internal transfers, four for external transfers
rows.note: Internal and external transfers also need at least two semesters in Arts & Sciences. Approved off-campus programs count for only some of them (two for first-year entrants and internal transfers, one for external transfers).

rows.label: Complete your last full-time semester (the last one needing 9 or more credits) in residence
Take two first-year writing seminars
rows.note: A seminar used here cannot also fill any other college or major requirement. ENGL 2860 or 2880 counts as a seminar only when you answer that you are using it for that purpose (it then counts nowhere else). A qualifying AP or IB exam score can replace one seminar, which the board does not track.

rows.label: Foreign language (Option 1 or Option 2)
rows.note: Overlay: language courses may also fill distribution or major rows. AP/IB credit never completes it. The native-competence exemption is not checkable (confirm with an advisor).

rows.label: Option 1: one FLOPI-AS course at the 2000 level or above, 3+ credits
Option 2: 11 credits in one language at Cornell
rows.note: One subject stands in for one language. Only single-language subjects are listed (multi-language subjects such as ASRC, CLASS, JWST are left out) and only courses tagged FL-AG, FLOPI-AS or OCL-IL count, so English-taught courses in a language department do not. The course-sequence condition is not checkable. A few elementary courses the roster leaves untagged will not count here (a false red, never a false green).

rows.label: Cover the 10 distribution categories with 8 courses of at least 3 credits
rows.note: Only Cornell courses count (no AP, test or placement credit). Transfer credit from regular full-time semesters elsewhere can count for transfer students, which this row leaves out to stay on the safe side. Variable-credit and independent study courses are left out. A writing seminar never counts here, even one beyond the two the writing row uses.

rows.label: Complete all requirements of at least one Arts & Sciences major
rows.note: The major's own rules are checked in the major layer.

source.anchor: Restrictions on Applying Cornell Courses to the Distribution Requirements

questions.quote: First-year writing seminars and ENGL 2860 Creative, Lyric, and Expository Writing or ENGL 2880 Expository Writing taken to satisfy a first-year writing seminar requirement may not count toward any other college or major requirement.
